authority: New Mexico Regulation & Licensing Department, Construction Industries Division (CID)
notes: CID licenses contractors by classification (e.g. GB-2, GB-98, EE-98J). I fetched the CID page at rld.nm.gov/construction-industries/, which sends people to the PSI lookup for verification. The fields listed are from an RLD statement that PSI shows names, addresses, phones and classification; I did not inspect PSI results myself. I found no bulk file. RLD runs a Salesforce 'Purchase a List of Licensed Individuals' portal (https://nmrldlpi.my.site.com/bcd/s/license-list-request), but it would not render without JS, so I could not confirm that it covers CID or what it costs. Public-records route is IPRA: https://www.rld.nm.gov/about-us/public-information-hub/inspection-of-public-records/

authority: New Mexico Real Estate Commission (NM Regulation & Licensing Department)
notes: The Commission page (fetched) links 'Purchase a List of Licensed Individuals' at this URL. It is a Salesforce page that returned only a JS/CSS error, so price, format and contents are not established. Per-licence lookup: https://nmrldlpi.my.site.com/bcd/s/rld-public-search?language=en_US (returns 200). Contact: RLDRealEstate.Comsn@rld.nm.gov, (505) 476-4622.

authority: None at state level (NYS Department of State states it does not license home improvement contractors)
notes: Fetched DOS page says 'New York State does not license home improvement contractors.' It names local licensing jurisdictions: New York City, Suffolk, Nassau, Westchester, Putnam and Rockland counties, and the City of Buffalo. So there is no state general-contractor register. I did not establish whether any construction trade is licensed at state level; trade licensing is local in the places DOS names.

authority: New York State Department of State, Division of Licensing Services
notes: Open Data NY dataset yg7h-zjbf, 'Active Real Estate Salespersons and Brokers'. Columns: License Number, License Type, License Holder Name, License Expiration Date, Business Name, Business Address 1/2, City, State, Zip, County. It holds ACTIVE licences only and has no status column; being in the file implies active. Each row is either an individual or a business licensee. Metadata and count were read through the API, and the CSV link returns 200; I did not download the file. data.ny.gov also has user-made derived views (e.g. 9twf-9yig, x6eg-w668); use yg7h-zjbf, the DOS-attributed source.

authority: North Carolina Licensing Board for General Contractors (NCLBGC)
notes: The search form classifications are: Building, Residential, Highway, Public Utilities (with PU sub-types), H (Grading & Excavating), S specialties (Roofing, Swimming Pools, Masonry, Concrete, Asbestos, Insulation, Interior, Marine, Metal Erection, Railroad, Sign/Billboard, Sidewalk Curb & Gutter, Wind Turbine, Boring & Tunneling), Unclassified, Accredited Builder, and Accredited Master Builder. It searches by licence number, qualifier number, company, name, address and phone. I found no bulk list. nclbgc.org returned 403 to automated fetch; the portal returned 200. Other boards license trades separately: the State Board of Examiners of Plumbing, Heating & Fire Sprinkler Contractors (public.nclicensing.org) and the electrical board. Records-request route not established.

authority: North Carolina Real Estate Commission (NCREC)
cadence: twice monthly for the $15 list (compiled 3rd business day after the 1st and 15th); daily for the $250/yr SFTP subscription
notes: 'NCREC Licensee List' costs $15 per list. Its fields are License No., Licensee Name, Broker Level, Firm, Address, City, State, Zip, BIC Name, County, Status. There is also a data subscription at $250/yr (prorated, renews July 1): CSV files updated daily over SFTP, covering licensees, licensed companies, trade names and affiliations. Per-licence lookup: https://license.ncrec.gov/ncrec/oecgi3.exe/O4W_LIC_SEARCH_NEW. Expiry field not confirmed.

authority: North Dakota Secretary of State (contractor licensing)
notes: A contractor licence is required when a job exceeds $4,000. Licence classes A–D are set by maximum job value (A over $500k; B up to $500k; C up to $300k; D up to $100k). The 'Contractor Records' data list (active contractors) costs $40 one-time or $40/month and is ordered through FirstStop 'Data List Requests'. Fields not established. Per-licence lookup: https://firststop.sos.nd.gov/search/contractor. This covers all contractors, not specific trades; I did not verify separate electrical/plumbing boards.

authority: North Dakota Real Estate Commission
notes: Licensee Directory searches by last name, first name, company, city, state, zip and radius. I found no bulk file or list sale on realestatend.org. Records-request route not established.

authority: Ohio Construction Industry Licensing Board (OCILB), Ohio Department of Commerce, Division of Industrial Compliance
cadence: on demand (roster generated at request time)
notes: OCILB licenses only commercial trade contractors: Electrical (EL), HVAC (HV), Hydronics (HY), Plumbing (PL), Refrigeration (RE), plus Training Agency (TA). I found no state general-contractor licence; residential and general contractors are handled locally, which I did not verify further. The free roster generator produces a download of the selected licence types. The pre-built DownloadRoster.aspx page currently says 'no rosters available'. Output format and fields not established.

authority: Ohio Department of Commerce, Division of Real Estate & Professional Licensing (REPL)
cadence: daily (page says it is posted 'daily ... at 9 a.m.')
posted_date: 2026-09-25 (HTTP Last-Modified; older than the stated daily cadence)
notes: Linked as 'License Database' from the REPL 'Notice Regarding License Lookup' page. The file combines the old eLicense and new eLicense LPI systems and includes affiliations. The old eLicense lookup was retired 2025-10-16; the new lookup is https://elicense.lpi.ohio.gov/s/licenseshome. A HEAD request confirmed a 200 xlsx of 8,635,604 bytes; I did not download it, so columns are not established. The com.ohio.gov short URLs return 404; the working page is under /wps/portal/gov/com/.../notice-license-lookup. The legacy roster generator at elicense3.com.ohio.gov/Lookup/GenerateRoster.aspx also lists REPL rosters (no fee) but belongs to the retired system.

authority: Oklahoma Construction Industries Board (CIB)
notes: The fetched 'Are They Licensed?' page (https://oklahoma.gov/cib/consumers/are-they-licensed.html) lists searches for Building & Home Inspectors, Electrical, Mechanical and Plumbing licensees, plus a separate roofing contractor registration search at https://verify.cib.hbesystems.com/roofing/search. The GLSuite lookup returned 403 (Azure WAF, needs JS); the old cibverify.ok.gov now points there. I found no state general-contractor licence under CIB, but I did not fetch an official statement saying there is none. No bulk file found.

authority: Oklahoma Real Estate Commission (OREC)
notes: oklahoma.gov/orec 'Search for a Licensee' redirects to this Thentia Cloud lookup, which is JS-rendered, so I could not confirm its fields. I found no roster sale or bulk file on the OREC pages I fetched. Records route would be the Oklahoma Open Records Act via help@orec.ok.gov / (405) 521-3387; specific procedure not established.

authority: Oregon Construction Contractors Board (CCB)
notes: Dataset g77e-6bhs, 'CCB Active Licenses'. It has 24 columns, including license_number, license_type, county_code/county_name, lic_exp_date, orig_regis_date, bond and insurance details, full_name, address, rmi_name (Responsible Managing Individual) and endorsement_text. Active licences only, with no status column. It has 18 licence_type codes: RGC 30,515; RSC 7,534; CGC2 5,505; LBPR 4,385; CSC2 2,483; CGC1 2,288; CSC1 982; RLC 916; and so on. I found no published code list for them. Electrical and plumbing licences are issued separately by the Building Codes Division (dataset vhbr-cuaq, not examined). CCB also runs a self-service mailing-list export (Open Data Instructional Guide PDF); I could not parse it.

authority: Oregon Real Estate Agency (OREA)
notes: OREA licenses brokers, principal brokers, property managers and escrow. The fetched Current Licensee Information page (https://www.oregon.gov/rea/licensing/pages/current-licensees.aspx) offers no downloadable list. I found no OREA dataset on data.oregon.gov. For a roster, contact orea.info@rea.oregon.gov / (503) 378-4170; availability not established.

authority: Pennsylvania Office of Attorney General, Home Improvement Contractor (HIC) registration under HICPA
notes: Pennsylvania has no state general-contractor licence. The only state-level register is HIC registration, required for contractors doing $5,000+ a year in home improvements, and it is a registration, not a competency licence. The search filters on registration number, business name, primary applicant, address, city, state, zip, county, phone and type of work. Search results can be exported to .xlsx and show active registrations only; I saw no full-list export. The dashboard relaunched 2026-05-06. I did not establish state trade licensing (e.g. PA L&I contractor licensing page, not examined). Contact: hic@attorneygeneral.gov, 1-888-520-6680.

authority: Pennsylvania State Real Estate Commission (Department of State, Bureau of Professional and Occupational Affairs)
terms: fee ($71.00 setup + $0.005 per licensee for the standard all-licensee listing); registration required for online purchase
notes: BPOA sells licensee lists for all boards, including Real Estate. Online purchase through PALS covers active listings only. Stated fields: license number, name, city, county, certification date, expiration date. No phone or email. Contact: ra-listrequest@pa.gov. Per-licence lookup: https://www.pals.pa.gov/#!/page/search. I did not fetch any PA open-data (data.pa.gov) licensee dataset.

authority: Rhode Island Contractors' Registration and Licensing Board (CRLB), State Building Office
notes: Linked as 'View Quarterly List of Registrants/Licensees' from https://crb.ri.gov/consumer/search-registrantlicensee. The URL is timestamped, so it changes each quarter; re-resolve it from that page. CRLB registers contractors (registration, not an exam-based general-contractor licence) and licenses commercial roofers, home inspectors, underground utility, water filtration, well drilling and pump installers. HEAD request confirmed 200 xlsx; not downloaded, so columns not established. Per-licence search: https://crb.ri.gov/search/contractor-search. Electrical and plumbing trades are licensed elsewhere (not verified).

authority: Rhode Island Department of Business Regulation, Commercial Licensing – Real Estate
notes: DBR's 'Lookup a License' page (fetched, https://dbr.ri.gov/about-dbr/lookup-license) lists 'Generate a roster' under Commercial Licensing, the unit that includes Real Estate, linking to this Tyler portal. The portal is a JS single-page app; the fetch returned only a shell, so I could not confirm that a real-estate roster exists, whether it is free, or its format. If it works it would be an on-demand bulk roster. Per-licence lookup: https://ridbrprod-search.state-reg-eastern.tylerapp.com/ (returns 200).

authority: South Carolina Department of Labor, Licensing and Regulation (LLR): Contractor's Licensing Board (general & mechanical contractors) and Residential Builders Commission (residential builders/specialty)
terms: fee ($10 check per roster); redistribution restricted: SC Family Privacy Protection Act of 2002 bars commercial solicitation use, and the requester must sign a certification
notes: The 'Licensee List Request' form is linked from https://llr.sc.gov/clb/. It is LLR-wide: the requester picks the board and licence type and mails to PO Box 11329, Columbia SC 29211. Per-licence lookups: https://verify.llronline.com/LicLookup/Contractors/Contractor.aspx?div=69 (CLB) and https://verify.llronline.com/LicLookup/Resbu/Resbu.aspx?div=46 (Residential Builders); these redirected (302) under automated fetch. LLR also has a login-gated 'Bulk License Verification' service (https://eservice.llr.sc.gov/OnlineVerificationBulk) for checking lists of licences; it is not a register download. FOIA: FOIA@llr.sc.gov.

authority: South Carolina Real Estate Commission (SC LLR)
notes: The Commission page (https://llr.sc.gov/re/, fetched) links only the lookup (302 under automated fetch), licence certification and FOIA. It does not link the $10 LLR roster request form. That form is agency-wide with a board selector (https://llr.sc.gov/AboutUs/MediaCenter/pidocs/Statement_Compliance.pdf), but I did not confirm that a Real Estate roster is offered through it. FOIA route: FOIA@llr.sc.gov or mail to Kathy Burgess, 110 Centerview Dr, Columbia SC 29210; $21/hr search fee. The SC Family Privacy Protection Act commercial-solicitation ban would apply.
